Recommendation:
- R 49-1 (2013) — canonical id "R49-1"? The rules say "id (canonical, e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60")". For R 49-1, the canonical would be "R49-1". Edition: 2013. Hmm, "edition (int)" — 2013 is the year. For R60 certs, edition might be 2017 etc. Here R49-1 (2013) — edition 2013? The schema says edition is int. I'll use 2013. Amendment: null. Scheme: A. Accuracy classes: ["2"] or [2]? Accuracy class 2. I'll use ["2"]... Actually as a string "2" makes sense. Let me use ["2"].

Test reports:
- No. NMi-2652375-01 dated 24 May 2022, 29 pages. Role: type_evaluation_report (it's the OIML Type Evaluation Report — "represented by the sample(s) identified in the OIML Type Evaluation Report"). The report mentioned is "the associated report(s): No. NMi-2652375-01 dated 24 May 2022 that includes 29 pages." I'd say role: type_evaluation_report.

Revision history:
- Initial, 24 May 2022, Initial release. The schema says revision (string). "Initial" — the certificate says "Number R49/2013-A-NL1-22.01 revision 0". So revision "0", date 24 May 2022, changes "Initial release". In the table, revision column says "Initial". I'll use "0" as revision string with changes "Initial release" (or "Initial"). Maybe revision: "0", date: "2022-05-24", changes: "Initial release".

Characteristics:

Table 1 General characteristics:
- Measuring principle: Electromagnetic
- Accuracy class: 2
- Environmental class: M1 / O (installed outdoors)
- Electromagnetic environment: E1
- Temperature range ambient: -25 °C / +55 °C → {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C
- Water temperature class: T50 (+0,1 °C / +50 °C) → class T50, range {min: 0.1, max: 50} °C. Hmm. Water temperature class T50 is a class designation. I could record water_temperature_class: {value: "T50"} and water_temperature_range: {value: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit_symbol: "°C"}.
- Maximum admissible pressure (MAP): 1,6 MPa (16 bar) → value 1.6, unit MPa. Could add secondary 16 bar. I'll record maximum_admissible_pressure: {value: 1.6, unit_symbol: "MPa"} and maybe note 16 bar. Keep one canonical: maximum_admissible_pressure with value 1.6 MPa. Could also add as separate "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar"? That's noise. I'll just include the primary, maybe with footnote... no footnote. Maybe include both? Rules say don't fabricate; 16 bar is present. I could add value {min:16,max:16}? No. Keep one: maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa. Alternatively map: {"value": 1.6, "unit_symbol": "MPa"} plus "maximum_admissible_pressure_alternate": "16 bar"? I'll skip the alternate to be clean. Actually maybe I can represent as value 1.6 MPa and add a separate characteristic "maximum_admissible_pressure_alt" ... too noisy. Skip.

- Orientation: All positions (Horizontal, vertical or diagonal) → value string "All positions (horizontal, vertical or diagonal)"
- Flow profile sensitivity class: U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream) → value string "U0 and D0"
- Reverse flow: description text → value string describing.
- Pressure loss class: Δp 16 (0,16 bar) → value 0.16 bar; class Δp16. Record pressure_loss_class: {value: "Δp 16"} and pressure_loss: {value: 0.16, unit_symbol: "bar"}. Hmm, "Δp" contains a Unicode char, fine.
- Power supply: replaceable battery 3.6 V (operating range 2.9–3.7 V); DC mains 10.8–13.2 V.
  Split into:
  - power_supply_battery_voltage: {value: 3.6, unit_symbol: "V"}
  - battery_operating_range: {value: {min: 2.9, max: 3.7}, unit_symbol: "V"}
  - power_supply_mains_voltage: {value: {min: 10.8, max: 13.2}, unit_symbol: "V"} — DC mains. Add power_supply_type: "DC" maybe. The cert says "DC mains 10,8 – 13,2 V". So power_supply_type: DC? But battery also. I'll record:
    - power_supply: battery + DC mains (string)? Better to have structured:
    - battery_voltage: 3.6 V
    - battery_operating_range: {min 2.9, max 3.7} V
    - mains_voltage_range: {min 10.8, max 13.2} V
    - power_supply_type: "DC (mains) and replaceable battery"? Hmm. I'll do power_supply_type: {value: "battery / DC mains"}. Maybe skip type. Actually rule 3 example: power_supply_type: {value: "AC"}. Here it's DC. I'll add "power_supply_type": {"value": "DC mains or replaceable battery"}. Reasonable.

Table 2 Software identification:
- Bootloader version 1.06, CRC b4F9C9Ab
- Legally relevant firmware version 1.08, CRC AC406F7C
These are components? The software items. I could record in characteristics type_level:
- bootloader_version: {value: "1.06"}
- bootloader_crc_checksum: {value: "b4F9C9Ab"}
- firmware_version: {value: "1.08"}
- firmware_crc_checksum: {value: "AC406F7C"}
Or as components[] with role "software". The schema says components[] only if cert names sub-assemblies. Software items could be components with role "bootloader"/"legally relevant firmware". I think either works. I'll record as components with characteristics? Hmm, components have characteristics{} — sub-characteristics. Let me do:

components[]:
- {role: "bootloader", type_designations: ["1.06"], characteristics: {crc_checksum: "b4F9C9Ab"}}
- {role: "legally_relevant_firmware", type_designations: ["1.08"], characteristics: {crc_checksum: "AC406F7C"}}

Hmm, type_designations for software versions is a stretch but plausible. Alternatively keep in type_level characteristics. I think safer: record in type_level characteristics AND matrix_tables? The instruction: matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Table 2 fits into components or type_level. I'll do type_level characteristics: bootloader_version, bootloader_crc_checksum, firmware_version, firmware_crc_checksum. Also maybe a matrix_table "Software identification" preserving the table. That's duplicative but the schema encourages preserving. I'll include matrix_tables for Table 2 and Table 3 (Table 3 is the family table → also model_level). Table 4 also.

Actually let me think about the model family. Table 3: two meter sizes DN80/3" and DN100/4". Attributes per size:
- DN80/3": Ø 80 mm, Q1 0.25 m³/h, Q2 0.4 m³/h, Q3 100 m³/h, Q4 125 m³/h, Q3/Q1 ratio 400
- DN100/4": Ø 100 mm, Q1 0.4, Q2 0.64, Q3 160, Q4 200, ratio 400

So model_family models: DN80/3", DN100/4". model_level entries: diameter_inlet_outlet (mm), minimum_flow_rate q1 (m³/h), transitional_flow_rate q2, permanent_flow_rate q3, overload_flow_rate q4, ratio_q3_q1 (dimensionless, same for both — could be type_level, but it's part of matrix; since same value, could be type_level. I'll put in model_level matrix since it's a column of the table; or type_level since constant. I'll put q3_q1_ratio in model_level for completeness... Actually rule: detect varying attributes → model_level. Constant → type_level. Ratio 400 constant → type_level ratio_q3_over_q1: 400? But it's part of family table with values per row; both are 400. Hmm. The note says ratio Q3/Q1 is at least 40, and chosen value 400. I'll put it as model_level with both values 400 to preserve the table, or type_level. I'll go with model_level including ratio for each model — mirrors table. Actually cleaner: put in type_level since single value across all models. But the table shows it per row... I'll include it in model_level; harmless.

Table 4: Indicating device — DN80; DN100 share values: indicating range minimum value 999999.999 m³, verification scale interval 0.00001 m³. These are config_level (both models share same values) or type_level since constant across models. Since the table has "Meter size" DN80; DN100 with same values, it's constant across models → type_level. Record:
- indicating_range_minimum_value: {value: 999999.999, unit_symbol: "m³"}
- verification_scale_interval_minimum_resolution: {value: 0.00001, unit_symbol: "m³"}

model_family:
family_name: null (no explicit family name; "family of instruments" mentioned). Could set "MUT7000 family"? Don't fabricate — null.
models: [{"model_id": "DN80/3\""}, {"model_id": "DN100/4\""}]

Hmm, model_id with quote char. Use "DN80/3in"? Better keep as-is: "DN80/3\"" escaped in JSON. Fine.

matrix_tables:
1. name: "General characteristics of the family of instruments", columns: [meter_size, diameter_inlet_outlet, q1, q2, q3, q4, q3_q1_ratio], column_units: [null, "mm", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", null], rows with values. Footnotes: the note after the table about freely chosen flow rates → include as description or footnotes. I'll add description: "Flow rates Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 can be freely chosen provided Q3 and ratio Q3/Q1 selected from paragraph 4.1 of OIML R49-1:2013(E); Q1 and Q2 are minimum values with Q2/Q1 = 1.6; Q3 and Q4 are maximum values with Q4/Q3 = 1.25; ratio Q3/Q1 at least 40." Also constraints could be config_level? The note defines allowable variation — could be config_level entries: q2_q1_ratio: 1.6 minimum etc. Hmm, could add config_level:
- attribute: ratio_q2_over_q1, axis: "flow rate selection", condition "minimum values", value 1.6
That's getting noisy. I'll include in matrix_tables description and footnotes.

2. name: "Software identification", columns: [identification, software_version, crc_checksum, remarks], rows.

3. name: "General characteristics of the indicating device", columns: [meter_size, indicating_range_minimum_value, verification_scale_interval], rows.

4. Table 1 general characteristics — it's a 2-col table of attributes; fits type_level characteristics, no need for matrix table. Skip.

Footnotes: Table 2 has "(*)" marker: "The checksum is stated as a hexadecimal value." So footnotes: [{marker: "*", text: "The checksum is stated as a hexadecimal value."}]. And values referencing CRC checksum get footnote_markers ["*"].

- accuracy_class: "2"
- environmental_class: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" — value string "M1 / O", maybe note installed outdoors. I'll do value "M1 / O" with a separate? Keep "M1 / O" and add environmental_class_note? Simpler: value: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" as string. Fine.
